# @handamade/psi-tokens

OKLCH formula-based design tokens. Code is the source of truth; all artifacts generated.

## Machine-readable artifacts
- dist/resolved/{light,dark,acme,ember}.json: every token with OKLCH, hex, and derivation formula, plus the theme's `colorScheme` ("light" | "dark", D116)
- dist/guidance.json: variant intent, usage rules, state derivation, typography defaults, motion/layout/fonts notes, recipes, and the utility-class roster at `utilities.classes`
- dist/dtcg/{theme}.json: W3C DTCG format export
- dist/components/{name}.vars.css: component-token declarations (--psi-{component}-*)
- dist/scope-map.json: D46 token scopes — property groups, per-token scopes (semantic + component), scale-family scopes

## Rules for generated code
- Use semantic tokens (--psi-bg-*, --psi-fg-*, --psi-fill-*, --psi-border-*) in app CSS.
- Override --psi-{component}-* tokens for one-off component theming; never fork semantic tokens.
- Scales are pixel-true: --psi-space-8 is 8px (0.5rem). Typography: --psi-text-{size}-{lh}-{weight}.
- Themes: import base.css + {theme}.css + components.css + utilities.css; set data-psi-theme="{name}" ({light,dark,acme,ember}).
- Each theme's block also declares `color-scheme` from its base (light, acme: `light`; dark, ember: `dark`), so browser-drawn parts — date pickers, select lists, scrollbars — follow the theme, including in a sub-tree. It is the one theme declaration that is not a custom property; it fills no element (a theme still paints no background), and an unlayered `color-scheme` rule of your own, one in a layer declared after `psi.theme`, or an inline style overrides it; one in `@layer psi.base` does not. The page's own scrollbar and canvas follow `<html>`'s scheme, so a theme set on a wrapper below `<html>` changes that sub-tree only (D116).
- Foreground utilities (D94): `.psi-fg-<role>` sets `color: var(--psi-fg-<role>)` for every fg token (`psi-fg-primary`, `psi-fg-secondary`, `psi-fg-tertiary`, `psi-fg-on-accent`, `psi-fg-danger`, …). Like every utility it sits in `@layer psi.utilities` and beats a component's own colour.
- Scoped tokens bind only their declared property groups (D46): fg* → text properties, bg*/fill*/scrim* → surfaces, border* → borders, --psi-space-* → gaps/padding/margin. Cross-family bindings that are design decisions carry both scopes (fgDanger: text+border for error borders; fillAccent: surface+border for selected controls). The token build enforces component bindings; the repo's stylelint rule (psi/token-scopes) enforces first-party consumer CSS (component modules + apps/). External consumers aren't gated automatically — dist/scope-map.json carries the machine-readable scopes to lint against.

## Motion (--psi-motion-*, --psi-duration-*, --psi-ease-*)
- Bind a preset, picked by intent (D141). Each is two tokens that alias the scale:
  - feedback — --psi-motion-feedback-duration / -ease = 150ms, ease. A control answering a pointer or a key: colour, border, outline, a chevron's turn, a toggle's thumb.
  - move — --psi-motion-move-duration / -ease = 200ms, --psi-ease-soft. Something entering, leaving or changing size: a dialog, a drawer, a toast, a sidebar.
  - emphasis — --psi-motion-emphasis-duration / -ease = 350ms, ease. A deliberate change that draws the eye, such as Card's hoverLift.
- Example: transition: color var(--psi-motion-feedback-duration) var(--psi-motion-feedback-ease). A component's own motion token aliases a preset's half: --psi-app-shell-sidebar-duration: var(--psi-motion-move-duration).
- The scale underneath: durations 150/200/350/450/600ms; easings --psi-ease-standard, --psi-ease-in-out, --psi-ease-soft. Only Skeleton's infinite pulse (D86) and .psi-media-tint (D35) bind it directly.
- Never hardcode times or curves. Under prefers-reduced-motion, all --psi-duration-* zero out (D30), and every preset with them — no per-component opt-out needed.
- A theme's componentOverrides value for a *-duration key must be exactly var(--psi-duration-<step>) or var(--psi-motion-<preset>-duration); the theme gate refuses anything else, so no theme can break reduced motion.

## Layout (--psi-container-max, --psi-gutter, --psi-z-*)
- .psi-container: max-width 1312px, gutter 40px stepping to 24px under the md breakpoint.
- --psi-z-sticky (1), --psi-z-nav (100), --psi-z-overlay (1000), --psi-z-tooltip (1100). sticky is for elements that stack within their own local scroll container (e.g. a sticky table header), not above page chrome.
- Breakpoints (sm 560 / md 960) are build-time constants (D31), not CSS vars: `import { breakpoints } from "@handamade/psi-tokens/types"` for any @media-driven JS/CSS-in-JS.

## Focus ring (--psi-focus-ring-*)
- One ring for every focusable part (D82): `outline: var(--psi-focus-ring-width) solid <colour>` on `:focus-visible`, never on `:focus`, never a literal width or offset.
- --psi-focus-ring-width (2px). --psi-focus-ring-offset (2px) draws the ring outside the control. --psi-focus-ring-offset-inset (-2px) draws it inside, for a control whose outside ring would be clipped or would land on a neighbour: a text field, a tab, a menu item, a row in a list, a panel against the viewport edge.
- The colour is the component's own --psi-{component}-focus-ring in component CSS, and --psi-border-focus in app CSS. The three geometry tokens are independent px values, so an override on any sub-tree takes effect there; the inset offset is not derived from the width, so override both together.

## Typography: display, serif, mono, page heading
- Fluid display tier: --psi-display-{min}-{max}-{weight} (e.g. --psi-display-56-128-black), clamp-based and pixel-true at both endpoints; pair with the matching .psi-display-* utility class for tracking/uppercase.
- Serif and mono are first-class combo roles alongside sans: --psi-text-serif-{size}-{lh}-{weight} and --psi-text-mono-{size}-{lh}-{weight}, same naming shape as the sans scale.
- The display face also has a fixed text style: --psi-text-display-24-32-medium (D118), 24/32 medium in --psi-font-display. It is PageHeading's style. Unlike the fluid --psi-display-* tier, it has fixed px, no tracking and no uppercase. Its utility is .psi-text-display-24-32-medium; on a hand-written h1, also set margin 0.

## Scrims and borders
- --psi-scrim-soft/medium/heavy: bgPrimary-derived translucent overlays (0.25/0.35/0.82 alpha) for text-over-media legibility.
- --psi-border-faint: low-contrast hairline border (fgPrimary at 0.08 alpha), used by Card/NavBar and other bordered surfaces.
- --psi-border-control: the edge that alone identifies a control: an unchecked Checkbox or Radio (D106) and, since D120, the resting border of Input, Select and Textarea. fgPrimary at 0.55 alpha in light-based themes, 0.40 in dark-based, gated at 3:1 on bgPrimary and bgSecondary by `nonTextPairs` (WCAG 1.4.11). Bind it, not --psi-border-neutral (1.32-1.48:1), for any control identified by its outline alone; --psi-border-neutral is a decorative border. A consumer theme built with buildThemeCss is held to the same 3:1.
- --psi-border-control-hover: the field border on hover (Input, Select, Textarea; D120), a step darker than --psi-border-control: fgPrimary at 0.75 alpha in light-based themes, 0.60 in dark-based, also gated at 3:1 on bgPrimary and bgSecondary. Do not use --psi-border-strong (0.30) as a hover over --psi-border-control: it is lighter than the rest state. A theme that overrides --psi-border-control should override --psi-border-control-hover with it: the gate checks each at 3:1, not that hover stays darker.
- --psi-fill-control: the fill that alone identifies an unchecked control: the Switch track (D122), bound by --psi-switch-track-bg. A ref to --psi-border-control (fgPrimary at 0.55 alpha in light-based themes, 0.40 in dark-based), so the unchecked track and the unchecked checkbox outline are one ink. Gated at 3:1 on bgPrimary and bgSecondary, and the white thumb (--psi-fill-static-white) at 3:1 on it, by `nonTextPairs` (WCAG 1.4.11). Bind it, not --psi-fill-neutral4 (1.10-1.27:1), for a control identified by its fill alone; --psi-fill-neutral4 is an active or loading surface.
- --psi-fill-control-hover: the unchecked Switch track on hover, a step beyond --psi-fill-control: fgPrimary at 0.75 alpha in light-based themes, 0.55 in dark-based, gated the same way. A theme that overrides --psi-border-control, and so moves --psi-fill-control, should override this with it so hover stays a step beyond rest: the gate checks each at 3:1, not their order.

## Media tint (--psi-media-tint, .psi-media-tint)
- --psi-media-tint is a brand-defined filter chain (D35); apply the .psi-media-tint utility class to media elements to get a tinted-at-rest, true-color-on-hover/focus treatment, transitioning over --psi-duration-450 / --psi-ease-soft.

## Tabular numerals (--psi-font-variant-numeric, .psi-tabular)
- --psi-font-variant-numeric is tabular-nums (D62); apply the .psi-tabular utility class to numeric content for fixed-width digits that don't jitter between rows. Table's own numeric columns (TableCell/TableHeaderCell `numeric` prop) bind the token directly in CSS — reach for the utility class for numeric content outside Table.

## Text link (.psi-link, --psi-link-*)
- .psi-link styles any <a> as a text link (D119): --psi-link-fg (the accent) underlined at rest — the underline cannot be turned off, because the accent is ~2:1 against body text — thickening on hover as the colour mixes toward ink (--psi-link-fg-hover). :focus-visible draws the shared focus ring; [aria-current="page"] reads as plain medium-weight text with no underline. The font is inherited. The React Link applies this class; outside React, put it on your own anchor.

## Visually hidden (.psi-sr-only)
- .psi-sr-only hides content visually while keeping it in the accessibility tree — position/size/clip only, never display:none or visibility:hidden, so screen readers still announce it and it stays in the tab order if focusable. Use it for status-word prefixes, icon-only-control labels not carried by aria-label, or a native input replaced by a custom visual control.

## Dark-first brands
- A brand theme can declare `base: "dark"` (see ember) so its formulas derive from the dark palette instead of light — use this for brands whose primary surface is a dark canvas rather than treating dark as an inverted afterthought. `base` also sets the theme's `color-scheme` (D116).

## Brand fonts (D29)
- Font roles (sans/serif/mono/display) are brand-level. The DS ships no font files — consumers load each brand's webfonts themselves (e.g. ember: Archivo for display/sans, IBM Plex Serif/Mono).
- Brand font stacks fully apply when data-psi-theme is set on the root <html> element. In nested subtree theming, --psi-text-*/--psi-display-* combos keep the default stacks, since unregistered custom properties only substitute at :root.

## Component overrides (D34)
- A brand's theme file may declare `componentOverrides: Record<string, string>` (e.g. ember: button-font → mono, card-radius → 0, media-tint → its filter chain), emitted in the brand's own theme file (e.g. dist/ember.css) inside `@layer psi.components`. Prefer this over forking a component's CSS Module for brand-specific token values.
- Component tokens have two scopes (D139). **Colour** tokens (a `-bg`/`-fg`/`-border` key, or a value that reaches a semantic token or palette entry) are declared under `:where(:root, [data-psi-theme])`, so they re-resolve inside every nested theme. **Geometry, type and motion** tokens (everything else: `--psi-app-shell-sidebar-width`, `--psi-control-radius`, `--psi-navbar-gutter`, `--psi-button-radius`) are declared under `:where(:root)` only, so a nested `data-psi-theme` keeps the value of the page around it: the page theme's `componentOverrides`, or a value set at `:root` or on any ancestor. A page theme's colour overrides stay in the page theme: they were contrast-gated against its palette, not the sub-theme's.
- A geometry alias such as `--psi-button-radius: var(--psi-control-radius)` resolves where it is declared. A theme whose `componentOverrides` set a dial declares every geometry alias that reads it again in its own block, so the dial reaches them wherever the theme is applied. A dial set by hand on a narrower element, such as inline on a nested theme's element, does not reach its aliases: put it in a theme's `componentOverrides`, or set the aliases beside it.
- The scope gate refuses an override of a geometry token that binds a semantic token or palette entry (violation group `"page"`): it would carry the page's resolved colour into every nested theme.

## Deriving a brand from a prompt (`./generate`, D57)
- `import { parsePrompt, deriveTheme, serializeCustomerTheme } from "@handamade/psi-tokens/generate"` — a runtime subpath (`dist/generate`, compiled from `src/generate` via `tsc`), not a build-time script.
- `parsePrompt(prompt)` turns free text into a `BrandVector` (hue, chroma word, mode, radius rung, optional fonts, slug name). It is deterministic: an FNV-1a hash of the normalized prompt seeds a PRNG, so an unrecognised prompt still derives a coherent, repeatable vector instead of failing.
- `deriveTheme(vector)` returns a `DerivedPair` — light and dark members solved independently by binary-searching each text token's lightness until the full WCAG AA matrix (`wcagAAPairs`) passes. The guarantee is about the return value: `deriveTheme` never returns a theme that renders below AA, because it throws instead — when a token can't clear its target at any chroma, when a failure can't be traced to any of the four tokens it solves, when 40 escalation attempts are exhausted, and as a belt-and-braces residual check on the resolved pair.
- `serializeCustomerTheme(pair)` emits real `customers/<name>.ts` source (a `Palette`, two `SlotMap`s, solved `ThemeDef` overrides for each member, a control-radius `componentOverrides` entry) plus the two registry lines that add it to the customer theme map — `pnpm new-theme`'s single-mode, override-free scaffold extended to a pair, with the solved overrides `acmeOverrides` (`customers/acme.ts`) carries by hand.
- Lower-level helpers are also exported for callers that need one step in isolation: `fnv1a`, `seededRandom`, `buildBrandPalette`, `hexFor`, `contrastOf`, `solveL`, `isBrandVector`, and the `BrandVector`/`ChromaWord`/`RadiusRung` types plus `CHROMA_WORDS`/`RADIUS_RUNGS` constants.
- `isBrandVector` is the runtime guard for untrusted input (e.g. the `api/theme.ts` Vercel Function) — narrow before calling `deriveTheme`, never trust a client-supplied vector shape directly.

## Building a theme outside this repo (`./theme`, D81)
- `import { buildThemeCss, ThemeGateError } from "@handamade/psi-tokens/theme"` — `buildThemeCss(name, definition)` returns `{ css, warnings }` for a definition shaped like `customers/<name>.ts` (`palette`, `slots`, optional `base: "light" | "dark"`, `overrides`, `fonts`, `componentOverrides`). It runs the same gates as Psi's own build, through the same code (`src/theme/gate.ts`), and throws `ThemeGateError` (`contrastFailures`, `scopeViolations`) instead of returning a failing theme. The names `light` and `dark` are refused.
- Use it to keep a client brand in the client's repository: nothing client-named has to ship in this public package.
- The CSS is scoped to `[data-psi-theme="<name>"]`, never `:root`, so a `base: "dark"` theme can style a sub-tree such as a dark sidebar. It declares `color-scheme` from `base`, `light` when none is named (D116).
- `psi-theme <definition-module> --name <name> [--out <file.css>]` is the same build as a bin, for a consumer's build script. The module default-exports the definition. Exit codes: 0 built · 1 refused by a gate · 2 usage error.
- The token builders (`token`, `set`, `delta`, `cap`, `slot`, `ref`) and the definition types are re-exported from `./theme` for writing `overrides`.

Live MCP access to this data: see packages/mcp/llms.txt (hosted: https://psi.kurkin.de/mcp).
